detail.body: # A / B | Rank | Language Used | | :---------------------------------------------------------: | :-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------: | | ![null](https://d2gd6pc034wcta.cloudfront.net/tier/2.svg) | ![JAVA](https://shields.io/badge/java-JDK%2014-lightgray?logo=java&style=plastic&logoColor=white&labelColor=orange) | 🔗 [Problem #1008](https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/1008) ## Constraints | Time Limit | Memory Limit | | :--------: | :----------: | | 2 sec | 128MB | ## Problem Given two integers $A$ and $B$, write a program that outputs $A / B$. ## Input The first line gives $A$ and $B$. $(0 < A, B < 10)$ ## Output Print $A / B$ on the first line. It's correct as long as the absolute or relative error between the actual answer and the output value is at most $10^{-9}$. ## Cases ### Example 1 + Input ``` tc 1 3 ``` + Output ``` tc 0.33333333333333333333333333333333 ``` Allowing an error of up to $10^{-9}$ doesn't necessarily mean you must print exactly to the 9th decimal place. ### Example 2 + Input ``` tc 4 5 ``` + Output ``` tc 0.8 ``` # Solution An arithmetic problem following [Baekjoon 1000 A + B](/posts/2021/05/21/a1000) and [Baekjoon 1001 A - B](/posts/2021/05/21/a1001). Hard to get wrong. For JAVA, just be careful that when you divide with int, only the integer portion is returned, so you must declare the values as a floating-point type such as double before dividing. ## Full Source ``` java import java.io.BufferedReader; import java.io.IOException; import java.io.InputStreamReader; /** * Baekjoon problem #1008 algorithm class * * @author RWB * @see 1008 solution * @since 2021.06.09 Tue 10:23:59 */ public class Main { /** * Main function * * @param args: [String[]] arguments * * @throws IOException data input/output exception */ public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in)); String[] line = reader.readLine().split(" "); double a = Double.parseDouble(line[0]); double b = Double.parseDouble(line[1]); System.out.println(a / b); reader.close(); } } ``` ## Categories * Math * Implementation * Arithmetic
